items.stem: A team starts many items at once hoping to finish faster, but finishes fewer. Introducing a WIP limit typically helps because it:

options.text: Reduces multitasking and improves flow and cycle time
options.rationale: Correct: limiting WIP focuses the team and shortens cycle time.
WIP limits are about focus, not overtime.

options.text: Increases the number of items in progress
options.rationale: A WIP limit reduces items in progress.

options.text: Eliminates the need for a Definition of Done
options.rationale: WIP limits do not replace the Definition of Done.

items.explanation: Correct: limiting WIP focuses the team and shortens cycle time.

items.stem: In Scrum with Kanban, 'work item age' is most useful for:

options.text: Spotting items that have been in progress too long and may be stuck
options.rationale: Correct: work item age highlights aging, potentially blocked work.

options.text: Measuring how old the team members are
options.rationale: It refers to work items, not people.
That is throughput/velocity, not item age.

options.rationale: Correct: cycle time measures how long work takes to complete.
Correct: throughput measures how many items complete per period.
